ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-collector (emitter follower) NPN transistor circuit. The transistor collector is connected to the +15 V power supply; the base is driven by the input source labeled Vin on the left; the output Vout is taken from the emitter node; this emitter node is also grounded through a 1.5 kΩ resistor. Reasoning: The problem gives the input voltage Vin = 1.5 V, and the base-emitter forward voltage drop of a standard silicon NPN transistor is approximately VBE = 0.7 V. In a common-collector emitter follower, the output voltage is approximately equal to the emitter voltage, that is, Vout = VE ≈ VB - VBE. The base voltage VB = Vin = 1.5 V, so Vout ≈ 1.5 - 0.7 = 0.8 V.
